content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect transformation of Ambari usernames to lowercase before storing them in the database, which led to inconsistencies and potential conflicts when users tried to access or operate with usernames that differed only in case. This patch removes the lowercase transformation to maintain the original casing of usernames, ensuring uniqueness checks and retrieval operations can correctly differentiate between usernames, thus preserving the expected case sensitivity of usernames in the application.

buggy_stmts_infos.buggy_stmt: -    // store user name in lower case
-    userEntity.setUserName("username"); // use lower case with user entity
requestScheduleEntity.setCreateUser("createduser"); // use lower case user name with request schedule entity
userEntity.setUserName("createduser"); // use lower case user name with user entity
